_readme: The one description of what a crate repository is configured to be. script/apply-settings applies it with gh api and refuses a setting the API rejects, never silently skips it. script/check-settings reads the live settings back and fails on any difference, so a setting changed by hand in the web interface is a red run. Names here are provisional until calef's naming pass.

metadata.description: {crate}: a standalone Rust crate, proven with Kani, released through the shared workflows

descriptions._readme: A repository's own description, under its name without the owner, in place of metadata.description with {crate} filled in. helpers/settings_description.py refuses one that names nife; apply-settings writes it and check-settings reads it back.
descriptions.block_roster_contract: The block-device roster page: which drives are attached, written once by the kernel and read by a program that was granted the mapping. no_std, proven with Kani
descriptions.designware_mobile_storage: SD and eMMC driver logic for the Synopsys DesignWare Mobile Storage Host Controller: no_std, no unsafe, proven with Kani
descriptions.e1000e: Intel e1000e-family (82574L, I219) network controller logic: registers, descriptors and ring logic behind small traits, proven with Kani
descriptions.extensible_host_controller_interface: xHCI (USB 3) host controller logic as pure computation: register offsets and decode, TRBs, rings, contexts and port status, proven with Kani

actions._readme: Every third-party action the template itself uses is named in patterns_allowed, with an @* version suffix. A pattern without @ matches no reference: every caller workflow that uses a third-party action ends in startup_failure with empty referenced_workflows (measured on the canary with the bare names), and the same patterns with @* run. The template's one third-party action is taiki-e/install-action (check, weekly). sha_pinning_required makes GitHub refuse any workflow step that names an action by tag, the same rule script/lint holds for this repository; approval_policy is who needs a maintainer's click before a fork pull request runs workflows (measured on the canary and on this repository: first_time_contributors, the default).

owners._readme: The values that differ by the organization that owns the repository, merged over the ones above by helpers/settings_owner.py: a dictionary key by key, rulesets by name, anything else replaced. An owner with no entry here takes the values above as they are.

partsfoundry._readme: A crate repository in partsfoundry calls the reusable workflows of partsfoundry/crate-workflows, which a selected-actions allowlist admits only by a pattern. The team lives in partsfoundry, and the release app there is partsfoundry-smelter (actor_id 5911990, read from GET /apps/partsfoundry-smelter), which partsfoundry owns and which is installed on all of its repositories.

rulesets._readme: A repository-level tag ruleset is accepted (measured 2026-10-17 on the canary); a push-target ruleset refuses ref_name conditions. The only bypass actor is the nife-smelter app (actor_id 5053502), which the release workflow's tag job authenticates as. The GitHub Actions integration (15368) is refused as a bypass actor ('must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization'), so github.token cannot tag. The app is accepted once it is installed on the repository. A hand-made v* tag is refused with a 422; a tag that does not match v* is allowed.
